facebook.content_angle: Tumble turn underwater dolphin kicks — most club swimmers take 1-2 kicks off every wall and surrender the fastest metres in the pool before they even surface
facebook.post_text:
You're leaving free speed at every single wall. 🌊

Most club swimmers push off, take one or two dolphin kicks, and surface before they've even used the fastest phase of their entire lap.

The wall isn't a reset. It's a launch pad.

👉 Elite swimmers hold 2.1–2.4 m/s off a legal underwater phase — faster than any stroke tempo they can sustain above water
👉 Every extra underwater kick at race pace can shave 0.15–0.2 seconds per turn
👉 In a 400m freestyle that's 7 turns — the maths add up fast

If your kick is strong enough in open water, it's even more powerful off the wall. 💥

✔️ Aim for 5–7 streamlined dolphin kicks before surfacing on every turn
✔️ Keep your core tight and your streamline locked — a wide entry breaks it all
✔️ Drill it in training this autumn block so it becomes automatic under race pressure

Your turns are either costing you or banking you time. Which is it right now?
